title: A Inheritance for the Will
premise: Vesper Underhill, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder recorded in the cathedral's sealed crypt ledger has not yet occurred — the victim being the client himself, Aldous Fenwick. As Vesper decodes a cipher woven into centuries of burial records, he discovers the crypt's locked door hides not bodies but a trust fund controlled by the cathedral chapter, and that someone inside has been quietly rewriting history to steal an inheritance meant for Fenwick's disinherited daughter. The 'future' murder entry was planted to frame Vesper and flush out the true heir. In the end, Vesper exposes the corrupt canon behind it all, unlocks the crypt publicly, and — having spent his life among the dead — finally claims his own place among the living by taking in the orphaned heir.
about_author: B. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing deaths in English cathedral archives before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper, power, and the people history forgets.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Not-Yet
chapters.summary: Vesper Underhill, POV. A stranger named Aldous Fenwick arrives at the archive with an impossible request: prove that a murder dated three weeks from now hasn't happened yet. He pays triple in advance. Vesper, amused and unsettled, accepts. Beat: curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Locked Below the Nave
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. He examines the crypt ledger and finds an entry for Fenwick's murder, written in authentic period ink on authentic period vellum — impossible. The crypt itself has been sealed since 1847, key held only by the chapter. Beat: first chill of genuine wrongness.

chapters.title: The Client Who Waits
chapters.summary: Fenwick, POV. Fenwick reveals he believes someone means to kill him before his birthday, when a family trust matures. He trusts no lawyers, no police — only records. Vesper notices Fenwick flinches at every bell. Beat: fear beneath bravado.

chapters.title: Ink Before Its Time
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Laboratory analysis confirms the murder entry's materials are genuinely antique; the forgery is perfect or it isn't a forgery. Canon Precentor Harrow dismisses Vesper's questions as archival pedantry. Beat: institutional stonewalling.

chapters.title: A Daughter Written Out
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Digging into Fenwick's genealogy, Vesper finds a daughter, Maren, erased from every record after her mother's death — and a trust whose terms hinge on who is legally remembered. Beat: the theme of inheritance sharpens into motive.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Burial entries across two centuries contain marginalia that isn't decoration: a numeric cipher keyed to dates of death. Decoded fragments point to payments — regular, secret, ongoing. Beat: intellectual thrill, the hunt begins.

chapters.title: What the Bells Witnessed
chapters.summary: Sexton Cobb, POV. The old sexton knows more than he says: the crypt was opened once, decades ago, at night, by men still serving the chapter. He warns Vesper to stop. Beat: dread; the past is alive.

chapters.title: Three Weeks, Counting Down
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Fenwick misses a meeting; Vesper finds his hotel room searched but Fenwick alive, shaken, clutching a copied page of the cipher he stole from Vesper's desk. Trust fractures. Beat: paranoia sets in.

chapters.title: The Chapter's Quiet Men
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Two church lawyers visit, offering Vesper a generous research grant contingent on surrendering all copies of the crypt ledger. He refuses. That night his office is ransacked. Beat: the institution shows its teeth.

chapters.title: Maren Under the Gallery
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Introduced as a cathedral volunteer, Maren has spent years secretly researching her own erasure. She recognizes Fenwick's name in Vesper's notes. She doesn't tell him who she is. Beat: longing for belonging, guarded hope.

chapters.title: The Second Entry
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The cipher decodes further: a second future-dated entry — a murder dated the day after Fenwick's, victim unnamed, initials 'V.U.' Vesper realizes he isn't the detective; he's the next body. Beat: terror reframes everything.

chapters.title: Harrow's Sermon
chapters.summary: Canon Harrow, POV. Harrow preaches on the dead resting in peace while privately burning documents in the vestry. We learn the trust has funded the chapter's ambitions for generations — and that Harrow believes theft by paperwork is no sin at all. Beat: corruption dressed as piety.

chapters.title: A Confession in Vellum
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The oldest cipher layer resolves into a dying verger's confession from 1847: the crypt holds no plague dead but the trust's founding deeds, hidden from the family it was stolen from. Every generation of chapter leadership has renewed the lie. Beat: scale of the betrayal revealed.

chapters.title: The Meeting at the Lychgate
chapters.summary: Fenwick, POV. Fenwick meets an anonymous informant who promises proof of who is rewriting the ledger. It's a trap; he escapes wounded, convinced now that Vesper set him up. Beat: alliances collapse.

chapters.title: Accused
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Police arrive: Fenwick has accused Vesper of fraud and conspiracy. Vesper's access is revoked; the archive seals around him like a tomb. Only Maren offers help — finally revealing she is the erased daughter. Beat: rock bottom, then an unexpected hand.

chapters.title: Two Archivists
chapters.summary: Vesper and Maren, alternating POV. Working from Maren's hidden copies, they reconstruct the full cipher and identify the hand that forged the future entries: not Harrow's, but the mild-mannered registrar, Pell, acting under Harrow's orders. Beat: partnership, warmth amid danger.

chapters.title: The Night Key
chapters.summary: Cobb, POV. The sexton, shamed by his long silence, gives them the crypt key he has kept for forty years. He tells them the date the door last opened — the same date as Fenwick's prophesied murder. Beat: the past chooses a side.

chapters.title: Below the Cathedral
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. On the appointed night, Vesper descends alone to draw out the killers, finding the crypt lit and waiting: Pell with a knife, Harrow with a lawyer's smile, and Fenwick bound — alive because a live accuser serves them better than a corpse. Beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: The Murder That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Climax. Pell moves to make the ledger's prophecy true; Maren arrives with police she summoned using the decoded payment records. In the struggle the founding deeds are scattered into torchlight — read aloud, witnessed, undeniable. Harrow falls; Pell confesses. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Reading of the Deeds
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The trust is legally restored. Maren is entered back into the record in Vesper's own careful hand — the first name he has ever added rather than catalogued. Fenwick, chastened, asks her forgiveness; she neither grants nor refuses it. Beat: inheritance reclaimed, imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Open Crypt
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The crypt opens to the public for the first time in 180 years. Visitors file past the deeds, now framed. Vesper watches strangers touch the history he saved and feels something unfamiliar: he belongs here, among the living who came to look. Beat: quiet joy.

chapters.title: An Entry in Full Ink
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Epilogue. Vesper takes in Maren as apprentice archivist, and together they begin a new ledger — one page left deliberately blank, headed with tomorrow's date and nothing else. Some futures, he writes, should be left unwritten. Beat: peace, and an open door.
